title: t18929: feat(lifecycle): let a session relinquish its own run so explicit removal of its finished tree succeeds
body:
## Summary

Adds worker-registry.py relinquish-session: the owning session (runtime PID must be an ancestor of the command; session ID selects its one run, recomputed as admission does) records an ended observation for its own run on a tree. worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree relinquishes and retries once only on opt-in (WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1) plus a waiting-for-caller result; worktree-helper.sh remove opts in, Pulse and release cleanup do not. Plugin guidance for session-owner-already-ended; CLEANUP.md documents the verb (reflowed to stay within the 500-line Markdown limit).



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs, .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md, .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cli_errors.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/session.py

## Decisions

Relinquish is permanent (re-admission refuses with session-owner-already-ended) and only ever selects the caller's own session run, so a sibling session of the same app still blocks retirement. The registry returns waiting-for-caller as exit 0 with a status mapping, so the retry gate keys on rc=0 plus the JSON status. The full-loop complete handoff also holds a legacy owner PID checked by Pulse (_worktree_owner_alive), so wiring relinquish there is a separate follow-up rather than part of this PR.

title: t18930: relinquish session ownership at full-loop complete handoff (GH#37448)
body:
## Summary

`full-loop-helper.sh complete` now ends the calling interactive session's own hold on its finished worktree. Guarded cleanup can then retire merged trees while the shared OpenCode app process is still running.

## Why

Every OpenCode session runs under one app PID. After `complete`, a merged worktree stayed pinned by two holds until the app quit:

1. The worker-lifecycle registry run for the session (`relinquish-session` was only reachable through explicit removal, from t18929 / #37449).
2. The cleanup receipt's live owner lease (released only after 4 hours, or when the same session registered a newer tree).

Long-running interactive sessions kept the live worktree count above the 200 cap. Pulse dispatch then stalled, logging `Live worktree count N >= cap`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`: factored `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_status` out of `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_caller`, and added the public best-effort `worker_lifecycle_relinquish_session <worktree>`. It uses the plugin-declared `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID`, and the registry still requires that PID to be an ancestor.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: added `full_loop_mark_cleanup_owner_relinquished`, which runs under the receipt lock and writes atomically. Only the exact receipt owner (PID, process identity and a declared, non-fallback session) can record. Also added `full_loop_cleanup_owner_relinquished`, a validator that fails closed on missing, partial or mismatched records.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`: `_clean_deferred_owner_lease_expired` now accepts `session-relinquished` before `lease-aged` and `session-moved-on`. It still releases only the exact post-merge registry contract, and every registry retirement check still applies.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`: `cmd_complete` calls `_full_loop_relinquish_completed_session` after the durable handoff and prints `Session handoff: registry-run=<status> cleanup-lease=<status>`. Headless runtimes skip it, because they exit at completion anyway. `cmd_finalize_receipt` (the final step of direct merge-wrapper flows) runs the same handoff on the receipt's worktree through `_full_loop_relinquish_finalized_session`.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: documents the handoff and the `session-owner-already-ended` refusal if a session re-admits the tree afterwards.

Nothing is removed directly. Every failure leaves the existing 4-hour lease and all registry checks in force.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: all PASS, including the 3 new cases:
  - a wrong owner cannot relinquish
  - a relinquished lease expires and releases only its own post-merge claim
  - an invalid record fails closed
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py`: 56 tests OK (2 skipped as before), including the new `test_complete_handoff_relinquishes_only_its_own_session`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`: passes. Its byte-for-byte `cmd_complete` handoff receipt comparisons are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh`: stops at `Merge blocked by t2449: trust metadata unavailable` both on this branch and on unmodified `main`, so the failure is in the local environment and not caused by this change.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts, and pinned `ruff==0.11.13` passes. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main` passes for function-complexity, nesting-depth and file-size.

- After adding the `finalize-receipt` handoff: `test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` and `test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh` (both call `cmd_finalize_receipt`) still exit 0. ShellCheck and the file-size and function-complexity ratchets still pass.

## Design note

`_merge_record_deferred_cleanup_owner` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` is intentionally unchanged. At merge time the session still needs the tree for release and finalization, so the handoff runs only at the two end-of-work commands.

Resolves #37448

title: GH#37446: fix: detect launched browser left stale by on-disk update
body:
## Summary

chromium-debug-use-helper.sh now records the browser install identity at launch (macOS framework Versions/Current target, otherwise executable inode:mtime via portable-stat) and compares it on launch reuse, launch-status, and every --profile command. stale-missing (running version's framework dir deleted, as Brave does on update) and stale-updated (install changed) print a restart warning on stderr; launch reuse reports LAUNCH=reused-stale and launch-status reports state stale with a disk= field. Legacy state files without a marker fall back to comparing the Versions/Current symlink mtime with the state file mtime. No automatic restart, because another session may be attached.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/chromium-debug-use-helper.sh, .agents/tools/browser/chromium-debug-use.md

## Decisions

Compare install identity recorded at launch rather than /json/version Browser vs CFBundleShortVersionString, because Brave's numbering differs (Chrome/157.0.8103.39 vs 1.99.55 vs framework dir 157.1.99.55). Warn only; never auto-restart.

## Regression Evidence

An automated regression is not practical here. The defect needs a live CDP-attached Chromium-family browser whose installed app bundle is replaced by a vendor update while it runs. CI runners have no such app bundle or updater, and simulating one would need a new fake-CDP-server harness that the existing `tests/test-chromium-debug-use.sh` does not provide. The stale decision is therefore runtime-verified on macOS against real Brave (below) by editing the recorded `disk_marker=` and the state-file mtime to each stale state. The existing suite (15/15) still passes, showing no regression in launch, reuse, or attach paths.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified against a real Brave 157.1.99.55 launch in an isolated profile root: fresh launch records disk_marker=framework:157.1.99.55, status disk=current, reuse LAUNCH=reused; faked missing version gives stale-missing warning on launch-status, launch (LAUNCH=reused-stale, rc 0) and --profile list; differing marker gives stale-updated; legacy no-marker state older/newer than Versions/Current gives stale-updated/current; launch-stop + launch clears it. shellcheck -x clean, /bin/bash 3.2 parse OK, pre-commit portable-stat and string-literal ratchets pass, tests/test-chromium-debug-use.sh 15/15.

Resolves #37446

title: GH#37406: fix: refuse gh comment --edit-last and add comment-edit by ID
body:
## Summary

Upstream gh picks the viewer's last comment from only the first 100 comments (comments(first: 100)), so --edit-last on longer threads can overwrite an unrelated older comment; the REST fallback also dropped the unknown flag and posted a new comment instead. New shared-gh-wrappers-comment-selector.sh refuses --edit-last, --delete-last and --create-if-none (including =value forms, ignoring the same text as a --body/--repo value). gh_issue_comment and gh_pr_comment call it before any transport, and the gh PATH shim calls it before resolving native gh, so raw gh, sourced wrappers and gh-write-helper all refuse with guidance. New gh-write-helper.sh issue|pr comment-edit <comment-id> --repo R --body-file F [--target N] reads the comment, refuses it unless the authenticated user authored it and (with --target) it belongs to that issue/PR, then applies the existing body validation, signature and privacy guards and PATCHes exactly that ID. gh-command-discipline.md gains the edit-by-ID rule.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md, .agents/scripts/gh, .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-comment-selector.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh

## Decisions

Named the lib shared-gh-wrappers-*.sh so hermetic test fixtures copy it automatically; the shim loads it optionally so existing partial shim fixtures keep working. Refusal rather than a safe --edit-last emulation, because 'last' is ambiguous across sessions; exact IDs are already the framework pattern (full-loop-helper-commit.sh, terminal-blocker-circuit.sh).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Refusals (no API call): gh-write-helper issue comment --edit-last rc=1, pr comment --delete-last rc=1, shim gh issue comment --create-if-none rc=2; --body --edit-last value allowed; invalid comment-edit args print usage rc=2. title: t18934: macOS input-activity row matching the Linux 5-minute input sampler
body:
## Summary

The profile README "Work with AI" table had no like-for-like measure across platforms. "Screen time (Mac)" is display-on time (knowledgeC backlit spans unioned with pmset display assertions, #37492). "Screen time (Linux)" is sampled human input with a 300s idle cut-off. This PR adds an "Input activity (Mac)" row measured with the Linux rule, and relabels the Linux row "Input activity (Linux)". The Linux row now says whether the latest sample saw desktop input, terminal input only, or a desktop whose idle time could not be read.

- macOS input evidence: `HIDIdleTime` on IOHIDSystem gives nanoseconds since the last keyboard, mouse or trackpad event. It needs no privacy permission and records no content. Measured on the maintainer Mac: two reads ~6s apart rose by ~6e9. `caffeinate -u -t 1` did not reset it, so declared user-activity assertions do not count as input.
- Lock and console rules match Linux: `IOConsoleLocked` true records `locked` (no input). A session that is not on the console (fast user switching) records `not-console-user` (no input). Unknown console state still counts, tagged `console-state-unknown`.
- The sampler is shared: `screen_time_linux_activity.py` takes a collector name (`linux-input-activity` / `macos-input-activity`), so intervals, pruning, the 300s cut-off and sampling-began notes are identical.
- Scheduling: macOS LaunchAgent `sh.aidevops.screen-activity-sampler` runs `screen-time-helper.sh sample` every 60s (RunAtLoad, Background, Nice 10), installed by `setup_screen_time_snapshot`.

Built on #37495 (merged as 3e4b802be5), which added `screen_time_sources.py`; this PR extends that module so the engine stays within its Qlty file-complexity budget. After the squash merge, `main` was merged into this branch (no force-push); `TODO.md` keeps one line per task, removing the issue-sync copies of t18933 and t18934 that duplicated the active-section lines.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_input.py (new), .agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py, .agents/scripts/screen_time_sources.py, .agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py, .agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh, .agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh, .agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18934-brief.md

## Decisions

- The test fixture `AIDEVOPS_HID_IDLE_FIXTURE` is a JSON file `{idle_seconds, locked, on_console}` rather than raw ioreg text. It drives lock and console states directly; the brief records the change.
- The Mac input row has no snapshot history. The activity log keeps 400 days of intervals, so `input-profile` reads it directly, and periods before the first sample show as unavailable with a "sampling began" note, as on Linux.
- Brief scope widened to `core-routines.sh` (routine description names the macOS sampler) and `test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` (module copy list, row label, evidence note).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low
- **Verification:** self-assessed. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`: 15/15 PASS (re-run on the tree merged with `main`, including t18932's history change). ## Summary

Splits the three oversized entrypoint functions in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` into named phase helpers. All code moves as-is, in the original order. | Function | Before (base `99ef92741`) | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `_pulse_execute_self_check` | 150 | 38 |
| `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline` | 255 | 13 |

- `_pulse_start_cycle_observation`: 1749–1761
- `_pulse_finish_idle_cycle`: shared terminal bookkeeping for 1777–1785 (preflight-failed) and 1787–1797 (stop flag)

- `_pulse_reexec_if_source_changed`: 1845–1878. It receives `_pw_self`, `_pw_mtime_loaded` and main's original `"$@"`, so `exec` gets the same argv.

Early `return`s that moved into helpers now set the caller's `_pw_skip_cycle=1` (and `_pw_skip_rc` for the mode runners). `main` then returns at the same point with the same code.

title: fix(pulse): overlap maintenance with dispatch admission (GH#37501)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37501

- Remove cycle-entry cache priming and pre-admission repaired-brief recovery.
- Reuse locked, resumable post-dispatch housekeeping as a background lane on Linux as well as launchd. Linux retains service ownership and joins after admission and instance-lock release.
- Apply an independent 300-second total budget and fair per-stage slices, including cache prime. Keep successful checkpoints across timeouts and retain the watchdog supervisor identity for lifecycle filtering.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: cycle scheduling and EXIT join integration, preserving the newly merged main-phase refactor.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`: existing lock/checkpoint/stage adapters, independent lane budget and service-owned join.
- Existing housekeeping and cache-prime regression scripts cover these changes.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified locally without launching real workers: housekeeping (38 checks), cache prime (12), conditional REST cache (34), wrapper characterization (54), first-wave dispatch suite, stage RC adapter and staggering (13). The production watchdog regression exercises total timeout/resume, distinct supervisor identity, and repeated scanner timeout without starving later stages. All seven selected suites passed again on final pushed head 60ebec042 after merging current main without rewriting published commits. Bash syntax, diff whitespace, commit ratchets and push hooks pass.

Local tool limits: ShellCheck wrapper cannot find its binary; `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` cross-platform-shellcheck covers the missing static check. Existing push verification defers TypeScript typecheck to CI because tsc is absent.

Unrelated verification limitation: unmodified `test-gh-shim.sh` exits 1 after its native-read attribution cases pass. The gh shim and all shim case files are unchanged from starting base 21ea5c240; this suite failure is not repaired in this PR.

## Decisions and remaining observations

The base already implements ETag/If-None-Match conditional snapshots, operation-specific gh native transport attribution, and bounded parallel worker admission (default min(6, slots)). Preserve those paths and all quota, claim, approval and launch-validation gates rather than replace them. Mode 0 now means service-owned background-and-join, not detached Linux descendants. A oneshot systemd timer still waits for its own service to exit; maintenance overlaps current-cycle admission, but this PR does not promise parallel instances of that timer service.

Production latency and target-worker capacity are NOT verified by local tests. The rolling timing window contains zero successful starts; undeployed production stage reports still show ceremony p50 above 120s. Post-deployment production observations remain necessary. No release or production restart was requested. Independent review identified inherited lock-reclaim and TERM-resistant descendant risks in shared helpers; they are not weakened or repaired here.

## Security review

Independent advisory review confirms that labels and workflow expressions alone do not enforce runner admission: a fork may edit workflow YAML to request the self-hosted label directly. The runbook explicitly forbids activation until non-bypassable admission controls and isolated disposable execution have been independently demonstrated. Same-repository branch writers are trusted by this design. Node expression modeling is not authentic GitHub Actions evaluation or evidence of host isolation.

## Runtime Testing

Repository-side expression tests only; not a claim of live runner verification.

## Outstanding acceptance and access boundary

The runner inventory API returns HTTP 403 for this account despite repository push permission. No pool was provisioned and no CI_RUNNER variable was changed. An authorized infrastructure executor must verify host disk headroom, demonstrate the admission boundary against malicious workflow changes, provision an isolated ephemeral repository pool, audit remaining workflows and reusable inputs, activate the variable only after those prerequisites pass, verify same-repository and fork jobs through the Actions API, and measure queue waits over 24 hours. title: GH#37514: pulse: resume stalled draft checkpoints via fleet re-arm and maintainer approvals
body:
## Summary

Stalled worker draft checkpoints no longer pause forever. (1) Fleet re-arm: once every runner has tried the head, _pcc_dispatch_stalled grants one exact-head continuation per window via the new _pcc_fleet_rearm_allowed. The window is AIDEVOPS_PCC_ATTENTION_REARM_SECONDS, anchored on the newer of the attention record and the latest stall release, doubled per further stall (max 2^6). It logs STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED ... mode=fleet window=<s>s, and the winner's fenced claim stops other runners in the same window. The per-PR fuse still stops it. (2) Maintainer resume route: pr_checkpoint_events.py / pr-checkpoint-revision.py accept stall-class releases (stall/timeout, stale_assignment_reset, worker_ownership_lost, worker_noop_zero_output, worker_incomplete_exit) and continuation-session clean/worker_complete exits as approvable closures. The released attempt is resolved as the single ready-lease owner before the release, so Pulse may release another runner's stale attempt. STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION now names the exact approval-template command. (3) pulse-dispatch-lib.sh _dispatch_draft_hint_boundary adds every doubled deadline from attention and CLAIM_RELEASED anchors, so negative-cache hints wake at the fleet window. title: fix(setup): detect installed OpenCode major version before plugin registration
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## Summary

On machines whose only OpenCode binary is the v2 runtime, every framework
setup/update re-wrote the v1-contract plugin entry into the global config and
re-created an auto-discovery symlink resolving to the v1 package-root
`index.mjs` (no default export). OpenCode v2 then fails to load the plugin:

```
PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
```

This change wires the installed binary's major version into setup-time plugin
registration:

- With no explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE`, detect the resolved global
  `opencode` binary's major version (bounded, numeric-output check) and run one
  global registration pass under the **detected** contract. Major >= 2 uses the
  `plugins` key with the `v2-plugin` URL; major 1 keeps the existing v1 behavior
  unchanged. Explicit env still wins (preview/override semantics preserved).
- Fix the cross-key merge-prune so consolidation no longer orphans the only
  valid v2 registration (the bare `v2-plugin` URL now survives).
- Gate `chmod 700` to aidevops-managed v2 config roots, so a knob-redirected
  user-owned config home keeps its permissions.
- Resolve the `opencode` fallback binary when the `opencode2` shim is absent.
- Add a degrade-safe guard (`declare -F`) so a stale deployed
  `shared-constants.sh` falls back to the previous v1 path instead of producing
  new breakage.

Files: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`,
`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`,
`.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh`,
`.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`.

## Linked issue

Ref #35902 — non-closing reference to the OpenCode 2.x V2 parity parent tracker.
This PR addresses one V2-parity gap (setup-time registration on v2-only
machines); it does not complete or close the tracker.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor

## Runtime Testing

**Testing level:** `runtime-verified`

Verification executed the real setup module in a sandboxed fake-HOME harness
plus the repo's shell test/gate suite. A live host-wide
`setup.sh --stage ai-session` rerun was intentionally not performed (it would
disturb the running session); the sandbox runner exercises the same module code
paths.

| Check | Result | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Dev environment started | N/A | Shell/setup change; no app server or UI surface |
| Smoke pages loaded | N/A | No web surface involved |
| Stability check (no reload loops) | pass | Idempotent rerun scenario produces a single registration, no duplicate keys, no symlink re-creation |
| Key user flow | pass | Global config retains `plugins=[v2-plugin]`, no v1 `plugin` key, no package-root discovery symlink across all scenarios |

Additional gates:

- `bash -n` clean on all three changed shell files.
- ShellCheck: zero violations on all changed files.
- Extended `test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh`: pass (version-detection
  fallbacks, env precedence, module-level jq-fixture contract, detection-only
  global contract, idempotent rerun).
- Sandboxed fake-HOME acceptance scenarios, all pass:
  - A — no-env, v2-only machine, v1-broken starting config
  - A2 — idempotent rerun of A
  - B — explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v2`
  - C — dual-binary machine: detection-only global pass keeps the v1 contract
    while the env-selected v2 pass stays isolated
  - D — explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1` rollback preserved

**Escalation warnings** (require runtime-verified level — satisfied above):

- [x] Changes environment variables or secrets handling — the fix changes how
  `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` and the `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_*` knobs are used at
  setup time. Justification: scenarios A/B/C/D above explicitly cover no-env,
  env=v2, dual-machine detection, and env=v1 override/rollback, plus shell
  precedence tests for the detection helper.
- [x] Affects production deploy or release pipeline — `setup.sh` runs on every
  install/update. Justification: the module-level jq-fixture contract test and
  the A/A2/B/C/D sandbox scenarios verify both the v1 and v2 global-contract
  paths and the isolated v2 pass without a full host reinstall.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR body includes a linked issue reference using `Ref #NNN`
- [x] I have followed the commit message conventions
- [x] I have updated documentation if needed (`tools/opencode/opencode.md`
  detection semantics)

title: t18938: fix: rotate the dead-stamp reaper so every claim stamp is reached
body:
## Summary

The pulse dead-stamp reaper capped each cycle at 100 stamps over a fixed glob order, so it re-examined the same first 100 every cycle. With 394 local stamps, 294 were never reached. Their dead interactive claims stayed self-assigned and blocked auto-dispatch work as dedup_active_claim_unverified; two were observed blocked for 12 days while the pulse used 0 of 20 worker slots.

The fix persists a rotation cursor (.reap-cursor in the stamp directory, invisible to the *.json enumerators). A capped cycle records the last examined stamp; the next cycle resumes after it and wraps; a full pass clears the cursor. Every stamp is examined within ceil(N/limit) cycles. Unbounded scan-stale never reads or writes the cursor. The per-stamp body moves to _isc_examine_dead_stamp with its safety gates unchanged (hostname, PID/argv hash, recoverable worktree progress, lockdown, lookup failure).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18938-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - shellcheck on interactive-session-helper-scan.sh and tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh: clean.
- bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh: 30/30 pass, including the unchanged per-cycle cap test (Test 18). New Test 18b: with limit 1, a permanently preserved head stamp and a releasable stamp after it, two consecutive reaper calls release the second stamp; the old fixed-order loop never reaches it.
- Runtime proof (sandbox HOME, 5 synthetic preserved stamps, AIDEVOPS_DEAD_STAMP_REAP_LIMIT=2): consecutive real reaper runs logged rotation resumes after b, d, then wrapped; a run with limit 10 completed the pass and removed .reap-cursor; preserved stamps intact.
- Root-cause evidence (local, counts only): 394 stamps; the first 100 in glob order covered two owners entirely and 30 of 256 stamps of a third.
- Post-deploy check: pulse log shows Phase 1 examined-N lines with rotation resumes after, and the blocked claims release within 4 cycles.

title: GH#37527: snapshot isolated-DB attempt activity to stop false worker_noop_zero_output
body:
## Summary

Fixes a classification defect that recorded worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0 for attempts that did produce assistant output. Root cause, reproduced on origin/main a87d89219: _finalize_isolated_runtime_data in headless-runtime-helper.sh merges or discards the isolated OpenCode DB, deletes it and clears _WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH. classify_worker_exit (status-0 branch), the _exit_trap_handler session-count re-read and _hrff_worker_session_count (the external outcome the review-thread scanner reads) then fell back to the shared DB. For ephemeral roles (private workload, triage, model replay) and for db_merge_failed, the shared DB does not have the attempt rows, so the count was 0. Reproduction with one synthetic attempt: before finalization reason=clean session_count=1; after discard on main reason=worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0; after discard with this fix reason=clean session_count=1, which the EXIT trap records as worker_incomplete_exit, a failed outcome with an actionable cause instead of an infrastructure cooldown. Change: headless-runtime-failure.sh adds _hrff_snapshot_attempt_activity, which counts activity before merge or discard, bound to _WORKER_START_EPOCH_MS and adding up across invocations of one attempt. It also adds _hrff_resolved_attempt_activity_count, which returns the live isolated DB count plus the snapshot and reads the shared DB only when neither exists; the three readers now use it, and behaviour without a snapshot is unchanged. headless-runtime-helper.sh takes the snapshot in _finalize_isolated_runtime_data before merge or discard; only an integer is stored, so ephemeral roles still keep no session data. test-worker-exit-classifier.sh adds one discarded-isolated-DB case: activity snapshot gives clean, a zero snapshot gives noop, a stale snapshot is ignored. Cited attempts (diagnosing runner alex-solovyev): the failed records for 37359 (epoch 1794231671) and 37364 (epoch 1794233267) are not in the metrics log on this runner; they were recorded on another host whose worker logs are unreadable here. This runner ran its own attempts on both PRs (attempt IDs 1794231670 and 1794233405), both result=success activity=true, and posted the thread replies (13:42:59Z and 14:11:55Z), so no review thread was left unanswered. Each cited attempt is either the false zero reproduced here or a genuine no-output duplicate dispatch; telling them apart needs that host log. Scanner ownership, claim, permission and admission guards and the existing bounded infrastructure retry are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — test-worker-exit-classifier.sh: 61 passed 0 failed, including the new case. test-headless-runtime-failure-classification.sh: 120 run 0 failed. test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh: exit 0. test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh (exercises _finalize_isolated_runtime_data): exit 0. bash -n on the changed scripts: clean. Pre-commit ShellCheck ratchet passed; this runner has no real shellcheck binary, so the full ShellCheck pass is left to the CI code-quality job. Reproduction before/after: worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0 becomes clean session_count=1.

Resolves #37527

title: t18941: reduce pulse process identity fork overhead
body:
## Summary

For #37537 (t18941). Implementation checkpoint at `19480c456`; **whole-unit performance acceptance remains open. This PR intentionally stays draft.**

- Derive Linux process birth directly from procfs without per-call subprocesses.
- Preserve the existing SHA256(lstart) identity, so old and new reservation and dirty-queue readers agree in both directions.
- Memoise only plain `ASSIGNED:` blocking results by cycle, repository, issue and login. Never cache permission to dispatch, read-only checks, uncertain errors or stale-recovery mutation signals.
- Reset the cache after the instance lock on each real cycle, excluding canary/dry-run. An owner-PID check and unique cycle key prevent inherited worker environments from reusing expired cycle answers. Standalone calls take the original path without an added command-substitution fork.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`: retain the existing `process_birth` API and identity bytes used by `mark_dead_reservations` and dirty-queue leases. Parse `comm` as bytes and split after its last closing parenthesis. Read boot time afresh rather than retaining a value across clock steps. Non-Linux retains the existing `ps` fallback.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`: wrap only the mutating CLI assignment check; cache hits cannot permit dispatch or replay recovery writes.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: initialize the cycle-local cache under the existing instance lock.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` and `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-is-assigned.sh`: extend the existing suites with process-identity and cache-boundary regressions. Canonical Files Scope was corrected and re-read before these adjacent edits after the platform-evidence CI failure; no new harness or dependencies.

Call sites confirmed in `pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh:585` and `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:846`. Both can inspect an assigned candidate during a cycle. Normalization subsequently mutates ownership, which is why caching dispatch-permitting results would be unsafe.

No schema change, migration, new dependency, deployment, scheduling change or wait-loop change. Recovery and dirty-queue consumers need no edits because the persisted identity format is unchanged.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: **72 tests pass**, including four committed process-identity regression tests.
- Dirty-queue suite: **12 tests pass** with an in-memory launcher adaptation replacing its hard-coded `/bin/bash` with the runner's PATH-resolved Bash. The unchanged direct invocation has three subtest errors solely because `/bin/bash` does not exist on NixOS. The three relevant lease-ownership tests also pass without that adaptation.
- Existing shell suites pass: `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-is-assigned.sh` (26, including committed cycle-cache regression), `test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh` (8), `test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh` (11), `test-dispatch-dedup-maintainer-permission-block.sh`, `test-dispatch-dedup-no-auto-dispatch-block.sh` (12), `test-dispatch-dedup-multi-operator.sh` (10), and `test-parent-task-guard.sh` (23), all under `.agents/scripts/tests/` and run with Bash.
- Focused runtime checks: legacy/new hash parity for **685 live PIDs** on the final implementation (716 in an earlier pass); parity in UTC, EST/EDT and JST; Linux subprocess calls forbidden by a mock; missing/malformed procfs, non-UTF-8/spaces/closing-parentheses in comm; Darwin fallback; dirty-queue ownership retained for old/new identities and rejected for mismatches.
- Focused cache checks: identical blocker lookup invokes underlying guard once; separate issue/repo/login/cycle keys are isolated; truncation resets the cycle; exited cycle owners disable reuse; stale-recovery and dispatch-permitting results are re-evaluated; standalone behavior unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` and `git diff --check`: pass. `shfmt -d .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: clean. The helper's remaining shfmt differences and one repeated string literal are pre-existing, outside the new function.
- Pre-commit and pre-push hooks pass. The push verifier defers TypeScript checking to CI because `tsc`/JavaScript dev dependencies are unavailable on this runner; no TypeScript changes were made.

## Regression Evidence

The initial Platform Fix Regression Evidence check failed because the checkpoint had runtime checks but no committed test changes. This is repaired by four process-identity regressions in the existing Python suite and the cycle-cache boundary regression in the existing assignment suite. The exact repository gate now passes locally against the five-file change manifest (`platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh --title ... --body-file ... --files-file ...`). No rationale exemption or CI-policy change is used.

CodeFactor's B607/B603 annotations on the new legacy-comparison test were addressed by resolving native `ps` with `shutil.which`, bounding its timeout, and documenting the fixed read-only options/self PID/no-shell boundary with the same narrowly scoped B603 annotation pattern already used by this suite. Bandit is unavailable locally; remote CodeFactor covers that static check. The 72-test suite and changed-file lint were rerun after this repair.

### Mixed-version compatibility

Both old and new readers compare opaque hashes directly. A `proc:` prefix would therefore be unsafe for old readers. The Linux implementation instead derives the same `ctime(btime + start_ticks // CLK_TCK)` string as legacy procps `lstart`, then hashes the same stripped bytes. Runtime equality across live processes/time zones demonstrates both old-reader/new-writer and new-reader/old-writer compatibility without migration. Empty identities retain the consumers' existing conservative liveness behavior. Existing second-resolution and wall-clock-step limitations of the legacy format are not expanded into a new token schema.

### Performance evidence and unresolved acceptance

Live pulse baseline, 30 seconds, using the unit's actual systemd ControlGroup:

```text
BASELINE core=0.636 observed_processes=1006
292 bash pulse-wrapper.sh
147 bash gh
 53 bash pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
 29 python3 gh-transport-governor.py
 28 gh auth
 27 python3 github_auth_runtime.py
 27 gh api
```

Identical 200-call process-identity microbenchmark, including child CPU:

```text
legacy: wall=0.2896s cpu=0.2913s
procfs: wall=0.0130s cpu=0.0129s
```

This is approximately **95.6% less CPU for identity lookup**, not proof of a 50% reduction in the entire pulse unit. The live service runs the installed runtime, not this worktree. No comparable changed-runtime pulse unit/workload is available in this run, and no live-service deployment/restart has been performed. A second measurement of the unchanged service would not be valid after evidence. The whole-unit target remains unchecked; do not merge or close the issue on the microbenchmark alone.

Recovery: run the issue's 30-second sampler before/after on a benchmark-capable runner with an authorized isolated pulse workload using this exact revision; inspect process rows and prove whole-unit CPU at most half on comparable load. If it misses, continue profiling within the declared exclusions before marking ready. Preserve this branch/PR rather than restarting.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Component behavior is runtime-verified in isolated admission/lease and assignment checks. Whole-unit performance is **not verified**. Independent focused review identified boot-time caching and binary `comm` parsing concerns; both were fixed and rechecked. Canary cache initialization was moved after the side-effect-free return. No publication or live-service deployment has occurred.

title: fix(tabby): restore managed tabs without per-tab SSH probes
body:
## Summary

Bulk Tabby restores were reported to connect only a few tabs per invocation, with an unhelpful generic SSH/tmux probe error. Comparison with a working direct-SSH launcher identified an avoidable non-interactive inventory probe before every interactive attachment and a difference in explicit-key selection. The live desktop failure has not yet been reproduced here.

- Connect managed tabs directly through interactive SSH when no local legacy attachments require name resolution. A normal 20-tab restore now needs one initial inventory probe rather than 21, in addition to the 20 attachment connections.
- Preserve stable-identity leases, legacy duplicate/ambiguity checks, and the final server-side tmux identity/prefix check. Legacy attachments still require fresh inventory before connecting.
- Default explicit key selection to `IdentitiesOnly=yes`; add inventory-only `--identities-only` and `--no-identities-only` host options. Aliases without an explicit identity override or opt-in retain existing OpenSSH selection.
- Retry only transient read-only inventory failures, with four attempts and 2/4/8-second delays. Never replay uncertain session creation.
- Report sanitized authentication, host-key, identity-selection, tmux, and transport failure categories instead of raw SSH logs.

## Implementation context

- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_transport.py`: use the existing `local_legacy` check to retain inventory only for legacy resolution; keep the existing `attach_command` guard and held lease.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_config.py` and `.agents/scripts/tabby_host_inventory.py`: validate the optional boolean and transport it through fixed SSH argv options and existing host CRUD.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_remote.py`: classify failures privately and bound retries around read-only inventory, not mutations.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-sessions.py`: extend the existing unittest suite for 20-tab restore, repeat-restore deduplication, direct attachment, legacy refusal, transient recovery, and effective local OpenSSH identity selection.
- `.agents/tools/terminal/remote-sessions.md`: document identity options, probe behavior, retry limits, and authentication requirements.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-session-helper.sh`: **63 tests passed**, including the shell launcher smoke path.
- Local `ssh -G` tests verify `IdentitiesOnly` and identity-file selection against isolated configurations without connecting to a server.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: passed available checks; Markdown lint was skipped because markdownlint is not installed. Existing oversized-file warnings have no new regression.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- No SSH daemon settings, keys, user SSH configuration, existing sessions, or desktop deployment were changed by this implementation.

## Desktop validation still required

The fix must be installed on the machine running Tabby; updating the remote host alone does not change restore behavior. Initial inventory remains non-interactive and requires prepared agent/control-connection authentication. This PR does not claim that the live 20-tab restoration problem is verified solved.

After installing this branch on the Tabby desktop:

1. Confirm the configured host alias selects the intended key. If needed, use `aidevops tabby sessions host update <host-id> --identities-only` (this restricts configured identities; it does not select a key).
2. Run `aidevops tabby sessions restore <host-id>` and complete normal Tabby Run/authentication prompts.
3. Confirm all expected sessions attach with `aidevops tabby sessions list <host-id>`; repeat restore and confirm existing managed attachments are skipped.
4. If a probe still fails, use the sanitized failure category to distinguish authentication, identity, host-key, or server/channel-limit problems.

title: t18944: fix(pulse): round-robin repo cursor for review-thread and auto-decomposer scanners
body:
## Summary

The async housekeeping lane bounds each scanner to a 12s share (GH#37501 / #37506). _run_pr_review_thread_response_scanner and _run_auto_decomposer_scanner restarted at the first enabled repo every run, so they only ever reached the first 4-5 repos. Unresolved bot review threads in every later repo never got response workers, and stale parent tasks there were never decomposed. Both scanners now rotate the enabled slug list to start after a persisted cursor (~/.aidevops/logs/<scanner>/repo.cursor) and advance the cursor before scanning each repo, so a slow repo cannot pin traversal. Reference pattern: _run_post_merge_review_scanner, which already keeps a repo cursor and still completes under the slicing.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-review.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-scanner-repo-rotation.sh

## Decisions

Advance the cursor on start, not on completion. Completion-based cursors would retry a repo slower than the slice forever; scanners are idempotent, so a partial scan is safe and later repos are guaranteed coverage.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Production pulse.log (counts only), since #37506: pr_review_thread_response 0 completions / 7 timeouts at 12s (5 completions of 222-392s before); auto_decomposer_scanner 0 completions / 7 timeouts; post_merge_scanner (cursor-based) 6 completions. New test-pulse-scanner-repo-rotation.sh 3/3: covers rotation, wrap-around and stale-cursor fallback; for both scanners, a SIGKILL mid-repo (watchdog analogue) resumes after the killed repo on the next slice. test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh 39/39; ShellCheck clean. test-auto-decomposer-scanner.sh (1 FAIL) and test-auto-decomposer-per-parent-gate.sh (5 FAIL) fail identically on the base without this change (stale grep paths from earlier file splits); tracked separately.

title: t18949: fix(gh-transport): bounded delivery admission class so worker-bus relay reads are not starved by pacing
body:
## Summary

The worker-bus relay forwards new human comments, labels and closures to live worker sessions, but it almost never delivered: its log history has 1 sent line against 26 deferred or failed, and every attempt since v3.39.158 (7 of 7) was deferred_by=local_admission. Primary pacing (t18827, #36201) keeps one shared GCRA slot per credential; bulk pulse demand (about 22k REST reads/day) keeps that slot beyond the governor's 10s admission wait, so a caller with a few reads per cycle loses nearly every time. This adds AIDEVOPS_GH_ADMISSION_CLASS=delivery in gh_transport_capacity.capacity_wait: it skips only the even-spacing schedule, and only while remaining minus reserved is at least a quarter of the window limit (1250 of 5000). Delivery admissions do not advance the shared slot; their spend still lowers server-reported remaining, so bulk pacing tightens automatically. Unchanged for every class: server cooldowns, exhaustion, serialized revalidation and stale refresh, 100-concurrent and 900-points/min ceilings, and reservation accounting. The relay sets the class only on its own gh api reads; its shell gates (stop flag, rate-limit flag, breaker, deferrable REST priority) stay in force.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py, .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18949-brief.md

## Decisions

Floor at 25% of the window keeps the exhaustion protection from #36201 for scarce windows. An opt-in env class rather than a schema change keeps the admission DB contract unchanged; only the relay sets it.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py: 69 tests OK, including the new test_delivery_class_skips_pacing_only_above_floor (delivery admitted where a normal read is paced, shared slot unchanged, paced again at 1249 usable < 1250 floor). shellcheck worker-bus-relay-helper.sh clean. Runtime probe with the real governor from this branch, sandboxed AIDEVOPS_GH_TRANSPORT_STATE_DIR, native gh and a real GitHub REST GET, pacing slot pushed 600s ahead: normal read rc=75 attempted=false deferred_by=local_admission (local primary pacing); delivery read rc=0 attempted=true. Env probe: AIDEVOPS_GH_ADMISSION_CLASS=delivery prefixed on the timeout_sec shell function reaches the child process and does not leak into the caller.

Resolves #37570

title: t18950: fix(screen-time): run macOS input sampler at standard priority (GH#37588)
body:
## Summary

The per-minute macOS HIDIdleTime sampler (sh.aidevops.screen-activity-sampler, added in #37497) ran as a Background LaunchAgent. On a loaded Mac (load ~45-50 from concurrent headless sessions) the Darwin background policy starved it: one sample run outlived its 60 s StartInterval, and consecutive samples at 15:46:39Z and 15:57:11Z recorded evidence hid-idle-unavailable, so input-stats reported collection_status partial. ioreg itself returns in 0.01 s. This PR switches the sampler to ProcessType Standard, drops LowPriorityBackgroundIO and keeps Nice 10. _launchd_install_if_changed reloads existing agents on the next deploy. Also records t18951 / GH#37591 (profile publication worktree leak, found while verifying) in TODO.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18950-brief.md

## Decisions

Scope limited to the input sampler: the 6-hourly screen-time snapshot and the memory-pressure monitor keep Background because they are not per-minute input measurements and have no observed failure. Nice 10 kept: under nice alone the probe ran at full speed.

Review follow-up (CodeRabbit, schedulers.sh:513, valid): non-interactive updates refreshed the screen-time schedulers only when the snapshot agent was installed, so an installed sampler without a loaded snapshot agent would keep the old Background plist. In `28a5ace032`, `_should_setup_noninteractive_screen_time` also refreshes when the sampler itself is installed. The same commit drops the Linux-only limit on the profile README escape hatch. Its comment ("macOS reads the Knowledge DB directly at render time") has been false since #37497, because the "Input activity (Mac)" row depends on the same sampler. This mirrors the Linux rationale of GH#36709. Installs with none of the three schedulers are still skipped. Interactive setup already installs the snapshot and sampler unconditionally (setup.sh `setup_screen_time_snapshot`).

## Regression Evidence

Automated regression is not practical for this change. The defect is Darwin scheduler starvation of a `ProcessType=Background` LaunchAgent under sustained host load (~45-50). CI runners cannot reproduce it: Linux runners have no launchd, and hosted macOS runners neither load per-user LaunchAgents in an Aqua session nor reproduce the load. A unit test could only assert the plist string `ProcessType` = `Standard`. That would repeat the diff without exercising the failure, and it would add a test-only interface to `_setup_screen_activity_sampler_darwin`. Runtime evidence on the affected host stands in for it:

- Before: under `nice -n 10 taskpolicy -b` (the background policy launchd applies), the deployed `hid_idle_seconds()` + `console_root()` probe printed nothing within 240 s. The same probe under `nice -n 10` alone took 0.02-0.03 s. launchd samples at 15:46:39Z and 15:57:11Z recorded `hid-idle-unavailable`.
- After (plist installed from this branch via `_launchd_install_if_changed`): samples at 16:04:50Z, 16:05:51Z, 16:09:53Z and 16:24:59Z recorded `hid-idle`. `screen-time-helper.sh input-stats` reports `collection_status: ok`, and launchd `LastExitStatus` is 0.
- Rendered plist: `plutil -lint` OK. `shellcheck` is clean on `schedulers.sh` and `_runtime_helpers.sh`.
- Non-interactive gate, exercised with the real setup helpers against this Mac's launchd state (one-off driver that hides labels from `_launchd_has_agent`): snapshot hidden → `main` skips (the reviewed defect), branch refreshes. Snapshot and sampler hidden → branch refreshes through the profile README hatch. All three hidden → skip.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified on the maintainer Mac (v3.39.161, load ~46-50). Before: the deployed probe hid_idle_seconds()+console_root() took 0.02-0.03 s per read under nice -n 10, but under nice -n 10 taskpolicy -b (background policy) it printed nothing within 240 s; launchd samples at 15:46:39Z and 15:57:11Z recorded hid-idle-unavailable. Fix applied live by rendering the plist from this branch's _setup_screen_activity_sampler_darwin and installing it with the real _launchd_install_if_changed (plutil -lint OK). After: launchctl LastExitStatus 0, no sampler process still running at the next check, and consecutive samples at 16:04:50Z and 16:05:51Z (61 s apart) recorded evidence hid-idle. shellcheck clean.; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at bfce1f9ad28facaaf68363c294f7bb8b592ee774.

Resolves #37588

title: chore(deps): bump hono from 4.13.14 to 4.13.16
body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.14 to 4.13.16.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.16

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

mount() and app.mount() can forward a path that bypasses middleware scoped inside the mount prefix

Affects: mount() in hono/mount and app.mount(). A dynamic prefix such as /api/:tenant/* was removed by the length of the route pattern. The forwarded path was also re-normalized by the URL parser, so a decoded \ became / and .. collapsed. Both let a crafted request skip middleware scoped inside the mount prefix. Routes such as /assets* and duplicate parameter names now throw. GHSA-4m76-xfj5-7975

RegExpRouter skips wildcard middleware for certain route patterns and for paths with an encoded line terminator

Affects: RegExpRouter, including the default SmartRouter. Wildcard middleware was not applied in three cases: a parameter written as {[^/]+} in the middleware path only, a /prefix* route next to /prefix/* middleware, and a path with an encoded line terminator. RegExpRouter now covers the same routes as the other routers. Custom patterns that can match the empty string, such as {[0-9]*}, throw UnsupportedPathError. Regenerate PreparedRegExpRouter data. GHSA-h7mg-cq63-vhpq

validator('form') skips validation for multipart/form-data requests with extra parameters

Affects: validator('form') in hono/validator. A multipart/form-data request with an extra parameter such as charset was not recognized as a form. The validator then saw an empty object while the handler could read all fields. GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v

css helper does not escape a closing tag assembled from template parts and values, allowing HTML injection

Affects: css in hono/css. A </style> split between the template and a value, or between two values, was not escaped. Closing tags are now escaped after minification. GHSA-3gg2-335m-rxc6

csrf() does not check requests sent by hyperlink auditing (text/ping)

Affects: csrf() in hono/csrf. A POST sent by Chromium's <a ping> has the content type text/ping and was not checked against Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site. GHSA-46wx-v44x-9hh2

Users who rely on path-scoped middleware with mount(), wildcard middleware with the default router, validator('form'), the css helper with untrusted values, or csrf() are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

What's Changed

Bumps the actions group with 4 updates: [actions/github-script](https://github.com/actions/github-script), [SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action](https://github.com/sonarsource/sonarqube-scan-action), [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) and [anomalyco/opencode/github](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode). Updates `actions/github-script` from 8 to 9
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

What's Changed

  • Add ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID to user-agent string by @​Copilot in actions/github-script#695
  • ci: use deployment: false for integration test environments by @​salmanmkc in actions/github-script#712
  • feat!: add getOctokit to script context, upgrade @​actions/github v9, @​octokit/core v7, and related packages by @​salmanmkc in actions/github-script#700

Updates `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` from 4.39.1 to 4.39.2
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.3 - 04 Nov 2026

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

Updates `anomalyco/opencode/github` from 2.1.1 to 2.2.5
Release notes

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's releases.

v2.2.5

Highlights

  • Worktree and Shell Mode Shortcuts: Press ⌘⌥O on macOS or Ctrl+Alt+O on Windows and Linux to choose a worktree, and ⌘⌥B or Ctrl+Alt+B to choose its base branch. ⌘⇧X or Ctrl+Shift+X now toggles shell mode in the composer. (#60713)
  • Send Quotes From the Comment Popup: Hold ⌘ or Ctrl in the quote popup to turn its checkmark into send, or press ⌘Enter or Ctrl+Enter, to send just that quote and comment while leaving the rest of the composer untouched. (#60640)
  • Percentage Compaction Buffer: Set "compaction": { "buffer": "20%" } in opencode.json to keep a share of each model's context window free, so one setting fits models with small and large windows. Token counts still work. (#60647)

Core

Improvements

  • compaction.buffer accepts a percentage of the model's context window, such as "20%", in addition to a token count. (#60647)
  • When read misses because a folder is missing, the error names that folder and the nearest one that exists. (#60688)
  • When edit can't find oldString, the error shows the file's closest lines, or says the change is already there. (#60689)
  • Calls to a tool named bash now run as shell instead of failing, with the same permissions. A plugin tool actually named bash still takes precedence. (#60687)

Bug fixes

  • MCP servers that send stdio messages larger than 10 MiB no longer get disconnected, and large messages are read much faster. (#60694)
  • Idle locations no longer restart their MCP servers right after shutting down. (#60668)
  • Compaction now caps its prompt at the model's context window when the input limit is larger. (#60660)
  • LiteLLM context window errors now trigger compaction instead of stopping the session. (#60692)
  • Reasoning is no longer turned into plain text when you switch models or resume an interrupted response, which caused request errors on some providers. (#60498)

TUI

Bug fixes

  • The connect menu no longer lists MCP servers, which are managed in their own place. (#60675)

Desktop

Improvements

  • Added keyboard shortcuts to choose a worktree and its base branch, shown in tooltips, and a shortcut to toggle shell mode. The worktree path can be selected to copy the full directory. (#60713)
  • Hold ⌘ or Ctrl in the quote popup to send a quote and its comment directly. (#60640)
  • Added flat input surfaces and a compact input size. (#60598)

Bug fixes

  • The connect menu no longer lists MCP servers. (#60675)
  • Added the missing top inset to the search field in the recently closed menu. (#60652)

v2.2.4

Highlights

  • Persistent Desktop Terminals: Desktop terminals now belong to the session, survive server restarts with their scrollback, and stay synchronized with the TUI and other windows. Renamed terminals also keep their names across restarts. (#60346)
  • Publish Interactive Artifacts: Enable "experimental": { "artifacts": true } in opencode.json to let agents publish, update, and serve HTML or static artifacts through the built-in local provider or plugin-provided storage. (#60351)
  • Guided Claude Agent Setup: Select Claude Agent from the provider picker to copy claude auth login, install Claude Code, and verify the connection before continuing to model selection. (#60603)
  • Choose a Base Branch Quickly: While creating a worktree, open Choose base branch with ⌘⌥. on macOS or Ctrl+Alt+. on Windows and Linux. The command is also available in the command palette and Settings › Shortcuts. (#60579)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's changelog.

Changelog

Release notes for OpenCode V2, newest first.

v2.2.7 — 2026-11-10

Highlights

  • GitHub Copilot Auto: Pick Auto in the model picker when your Copilot account has an Auto pool, and Copilot's router chooses the model for each session at the Auto discount. If routing fails, OpenCode falls back to the account's default chat model. (#62997)
  • Side Panel Tab Shortcuts: Right-click a side panel tab and choose Close tabs to the right. ⌘W now closes side panel tabs wherever focus is, ⌥⌘W or Ctrl+Alt+W always closes the session tab, and ⌘⇧T reopens the last closed tab of either kind where it was. (#62922)
  • Mark Sessions Read or Unread: Open the menu on a tab, Home row, project row or inbox card and choose Mark as unread to keep its dot until you next visit. (#62889)

Breaking changes

@opencode/ai: ImageResponse.image is removed

This affects code that imports @opencode/ai directly. Read response.images[0] instead of response.image. (#63011)

SDK: fewer endpoints wait for plugins to load

On a Location that is still loading plugins, agent.list returns the agents loaded so far, and integration.list, usage.limits, vcs.init, rpc.call and artifact.* no longer wait up to 5 seconds. Entries and actions that a plugin provides appear when it finishes loading, so refresh on the matching *.updated event. Model, provider, generate.*, voice.* and websearch.query endpoints still wait. (#62796, #63040)

Core

Improvements

  • MCP Logins Stay Signed In: Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer sign you out when several clients refresh at once or the token endpoint fails for a moment. (#62827, #63012)
  • read accepts a negative offset to read from the end of a file, such as -50 for the last 50 lines. An offset past the end returns the last lines and the file's line count instead of failing. (#62147)
  • When read can't find a file, it suggests close names: different capitalization, another extension, a small typo, or the matching path inside the project. (#62147)
  • Shell results end with Exit code: N. Commands killed by a signal show the signal name, and timeouts say how long they waited and suggest a larger timeout. (#62141)
  • Prompt cache warming times its pings from the model's cache.ttl by default (interval: "auto"), or every 4 minutes without a TTL. Models whose cache outlasts the warming duration are no longer pinged. (#62831)
  • When MCP servers connect, disconnect or change tools, Code Mode sends the model a short list of what changed instead of the whole tool catalog. (#62176)

Bug fixes

  • GitHub Copilot session costs use the amount Copilot charged instead of the catalog estimate, and content-filter errors name the filter that blocked the response. (#62034)
  • GitHub Copilot picks up a new API endpoint after a plan change on its next model refresh, so you no longer have to sign in again. (#62171)
  • Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer log you out when the TUI, desktop app, background service or several projects refresh the same login at once. (#62827)
  • A temporary failure while refreshing an MCP OAuth token keeps your login for the next try instead of marking the server needs_auth. (#63012)
  • MCP tool calls no longer fail when the server's result doesn't match the tool's own output schema, so completed actions aren't reported as failed. (#61254)
  • MCP prompts stay available when refreshing a server's prompt list fails. (#62266)
  • With background_compaction on, a background summary no longer stops a running Claude Agent session mid tool call. (#63025)
  • After opencode auth logout on a .well-known integration, its remote providers and policies stop applying until you log back in. (#62760)
  • OpenCode Console workspace policies still apply when Console's instructions or skills fail to load. (#62702)
  • Cloudflare AI Gateway providers set up with only gatewayApiKey now send that key. (#62574)
  • A v1 model override that sets only some capabilities no longer resets the others, so catalog capabilities like PDF input are kept. (#62573)
  • A v1 provider config that sets both api and options.baseURL keeps options.baseURL. (#62570)
  • Legacy model references with an inline variant, such as "openai/gpt-5#high", keep the variant. (#62254)
  • A fresh install imports saved provider credentials from the legacy auth.json, and skips an invalid one with a warning instead of stopping setup. (#62568)
  • Cache warming stops for a session when a ping rebuilds the cache instead of reading it, counts its interval from when a request was sent, and no longer pings during compaction or after the session is deleted. (#62926, #62941, #62972)

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 9bbb8ce release: v2.2.5
  • 958f965 chore: refresh docs and provider ordering (#60731)
  • 171dbd6 feat(app): add worktree picker shortcuts and toggle shell mode (#60713)
  • 1a443ae fix(core): frame MCP stdio messages without the SDK read buffer (#60694)

title: fix(storage): reclaim Linux same-filesystem Trash candidates (GH#37617)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37617.

- Delete already-eligible Linux task scratch and ignored idle-worktree output when source and user Trash share a device.
- Preserve owner, identity, inactivity, Git, cwd, mount and nested-repository vetoes; retain native cleaner/Trash behavior for other devices and platforms.
- Document the policy in `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md`.

## Files and reference pattern

Scoped to `.agents/scripts/task-temp-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree-artefact-reclaim.sh`, `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md`, and existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-system-cleanup.sh` coverage. The existing pressure-deletion branch provides the safe recursive-deletion pattern.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — exact head `bdf4e7a45` on Linux, Python 3.13.17

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-system-cleanup.sh`: all 16 tests pass. Covers same-device deletion without pressure, missing/existing Trash, cross-device Trash, live-owner vetoes, malformed manifests, symlinks, exclusions, deadlines, partial backend failures and fallback revalidation.
- Isolated production `system-cleanup.sh --force` reproducer: allocated 33,554,432 bytes, observed free-space increase of 33,554,432 bytes; summary `eligible=1 trashed=0 deleted=1 failed=0 pressure=0`. No Trash directory created.
- Focused production artefact functions against a private Git fixture: ignored `node_modules` deleted, external symlink target untouched, nested repository retained. Synthetic mount-table checks confirm both helpers veto nested same-device bind mounts (including escaped paths) and unavailable mount evidence before deletion.
- `bash -n` passes for all three changed shell files; `git diff --check` passes. Pre-commit return/parameter/string/portable-stat and ShellCheck ratchet gates pass.
- Independent review found a nested-mount hazard in extending recursive deletion; repaired with fail-closed `/proc/self/mountinfo` checks in both helpers. Follow-up review found no further concrete defect. Mount checks are not an atomic defence against concurrent mount changes.

No host cleanup, credential changes, dependency installs or existing Trash expunging performed. Native macOS execution was not available; the new deletion paths are Linux-only.

Local tooling limitation: `shellcheck --version` reports no underlying binary. CI coverage is `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` / `cross-platform-shellcheck`; standalone ShellCheck is not claimed clean locally. The push hook defers `bun run typecheck` to CI because `tsc` is absent; no TypeScript files are changed.

## Decision

Choose option A to reclaim bytes immediately without a new Trash inventory/retention subsystem. Compare the source device to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash` (default user data location); when not yet created, use its nearest existing ancestor. Unknown evidence cannot authorize same-device deletion. Cross-device/platform handling and pressure ordering remain. Existing unrelated Trash is never emptied.

title: GH#37649: skip rate-limited providers in subagent routing
body:
## Summary

Subagent and primary routing now skip a provider whose OAuth pool is the active credential and has no usable account because every account is in a rate-limit cooldown (new provider-rate-limits.mjs, consulted by candidateRoutable via the existing availability object). The provider becomes routable again at the earliest cooldownUntil with no config change; a single recovered or active account keeps it routable. When no same-tier candidate remains, the routing error now names rate_limited=model@reset alongside entitlement rejections. Pins, local-only policy, specialist-advisor and lower-tier substitution rules are unchanged: the check only removes candidates. API-key providers and unreadable pools are unaffected (fail-open). Ripple: primary entitlement failover and A/B arm routing share candidateRoutable and also skip an exhausted pool during its cooldown.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-routing.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-rate-limits.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs

## Decisions

Part 2 of the approved plan (abort a child waiting in OpenCode retry and fail it over in-place) is intentionally not shipped, per the review's documented fallback. In OpenCode v1.19.5 session/tools.ts runs tool.execute.after only after item.execute succeeds, and tool/tool.ts wraps execution in Effect.orDie, so a cancelled or failed Task never reaches the V1 after-hook; the V2 adapter applies hook output only for status completed. Aborting would therefore turn a slow retry into an unexplained Task cancelled with no failover. Evidence is recorded on the issue.

title: GH#37663: feat(opencode): safe interrupt-maintain-resume for interactive TUI sessions
body:
## Summary

Adds .agents/scripts/opencode-session-restart-helper.sh (inventory/stop/resume/run/notify/notice). It inventories interactive OpenCode TUI holders from session-bus presence (kind tui), falling back to activity heartbeats for DB holders. Each holder gets PID, session ID, cwd, age, busy/idle state and tmux pane (TMUX_PANE or process ancestry), screen window or bare TTY. stop sends busy sessions a session-bus checkpoint request and waits for idle. It never signals a busy session. Idle TUIs get SIGTERM with no escalation, after their entry is written to a 0600 restart manifest. resume relaunches `cd <cwd> && opencode -s <id>` via tmux send-keys or screen stuff, leaves a resume command plus a session-start notice for bare TTYs, and posts a restart note to each session.
