title: t18961: fail over V2 Task children stuck in provider rate-limit retry (GH#37667)
body:
## Summary

OpenCode V2 retry hook now moves a running Task child to the next routable same-tier model when its provider's whole OAuth pool is rate limited. V2 reloads the session model before every retry attempt, so the plugin calls session.switchModel on the child and sets the retry delay to 0; the same Task run continues and the parent receives the child's normal result. Skipped for root sessions, pinned agents or models, specialist-advisor/domain-focused/domain-light, local-only policy, API-key providers, partially limited pools and terminal host decisions. Same tier only; with no candidate the host retry stands and the rate_limited=model@reset detail is logged. New module v2-subagent-failover.mjs owns tier/candidate selection, child-route guards and the host binding; v2.mjs only wires it after provider-auth account rotation. Reuses provider-rate-limits.mjs exhaustion detection (new resolveRoutingAvailability) and model-routing.mjs candidate primitives; routingUnavailableDetail moved to model-routing.mjs from subagent-effort-handlers.mjs so both callers share it.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-routing.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-rate-limits.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-subagent-failover.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs

## Decisions

Host error classification: a 429 whose message reads 'usage limit' is AI.Error.QuotaExceeded in V2 2.0.24 and is terminal (not retried), so the child fails at once with a Subagent failed error result rather than being stuck; this change intentionally acts only on host-scheduled retries (RateLimit), matching the issue scope. The logic lives in a new module because the inline version failed the Qlty smell regression gate (+6); the Files Scope on the issue was extended with that one path. subagent-effort.mjs still has an inline availability resolver equivalent to resolveRoutingAvailability; left untouched because it is outside the Files Scope.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: live product-path run on OpenCode V2 2.0.24 (opencode run --standalone) with isolated XDG dirs, this branch's v2-plugin, a fake OAuth pool whose only openai account is rate-limited for 3h, and a local OpenAI-compatible mock. Parent on openai/mock-a called the subagent tool; the child's first request got HTTP 429 rate_limit_exceeded with retry-after 3600; plugin log: 'Subagent rate-limit failover: session <child> openai/mock-a -> mockb/mock-b (standard tier)'; the next attempt (~190ms later) hit mockb/mock-b and the parent's subagent tool result was state=completed with the child's text. Re-run after the module refactor: same result. Negative control: mock-b only in the simple tier -> WARN 'found no routable standard model ... rate_limited=openai/mock-a@<reset>', no lower-tier switch, child stayed in host backoff (no further request for 20s until the run budget ended). Unit: node --test test-opencode-v2-adapter, test-subagent-effort, test-model-routing: 102 pass, 0 fail (3 GH#37667 tests cover the success path, the exclusion matrix and host binding); test-opencode-v2-adapter re-run after the CodeFactor spread fix: exit 0. commit-and-pr node validators (npm run test, plugin workspace): passed. linters-local.sh --base-ref origin/main: ALL LOCAL CHECKS PASSED.

Resolves #37667

title: GH#37554: fix(pulse): fail closed on unverified simplification creator instead of filing held issues
body:
## Summary

Root cause: `_complexity_scan_permission_gate` only ran its admin check when a bare `gh api user` returned a login. When that lookup resolved empty, the gate skipped the permission check entirely, the scan still ran, and every generated issue got `hold-for-review` (the empty login never matched the configured maintainer). Evidence: #37672 and #37554 were both authored by alex-solovyev, whose live collaborator permission is `write` (a successful gate would have skipped the scan), and both got `hold-for-review` within 1s of creation from the author. Nobody owns approving those holds, so the debt issue stranded, the debt count stalled, and the stall-sweep generator then filed #37554, which was held too and also carried an inferred `origin:interactive` without `auto-dispatch` (treated as a live interactive claim by `dispatch-dedup-assignment.sh`).

Systemic fix:
- `pulse-simplification-scan.sh` `_complexity_scan_permission_gate`: uses the credential-pinned `_gh_current_user_allows_repo_write` and **fails closed** (no issues created) when identity or admin authority is unverified. Any verified admin creates unheld issues; the configured-maintainer login comparison is gone.
- Stall review creator: explicit `auto-dispatch` + `origin:worker`.
- `_complexity_close_recovered_sweeps`: finds stall reviews by generator marker (`quality-debt` + title search), not `hold-for-review`, so unheld reviews are still closed when the stall recovers; reviews a worker is actively advancing are skipped.
- New `_complexity_release_creation_holds` (called each scan cycle after the gate): for open `hold-for-review` issues carrying a complexity generator marker, releases the hold (adds `auto-dispatch`) only when every `hold-for-review` label event was applied by the issue author within 300s of creation and the author has verified write authority (the same authority the dispatch gate admits). Later decision holds and other actors' holds are preserved.

Resolves #37554
issue #37672 (the pulse releases its hold after deploy; a worker then performs the doc simplification)



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-issues.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh

## Decisions

Kept the admin-only scanner role (single scanner per repo, GH#16786/GH#18197) rather than widening scan creation to write collaborators; write collaborators' pulses now skip the scan instead of filing held issues. Backfill trusts write authority because such an author could already file an unheld auto-dispatch issue that dispatch admits, so the release grants nothing new.

title: GH#37697: signed standing release policy for routine Cloudron upstream bumps
body:
## Summary

Root cause of the Cloudron release backlog: every package bump needed its own maintainer signature. aidevops-cloudron-app#251 sat unsigned for 8 days while r924 reported `NO_APPROVAL; no merge`.

This PR adds an optional, signed standing policy per repository:

- **Creating the policy:** `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh policy-request <repo>` creates an approval-only `release-standing-policy` issue. A maintainer signs it once with `sudo aidevops approve issue N <repo>`.
- **What it unlocks:** r924 then merges and publishes **unsigned** release requests (`NO_APPROVAL` only), but only when the fail-closed predicate `cloudron_routine_bump.py` proves the PR is a routine upstream bump. That requires all of:
  - an open, trusted monitor finding equal to `upstreamVersion`, with the same major (and the same minor under 0.x);
  - a patch-only package bump, with no other manifest change (type-exact comparison);
  - additions-only changelogs;
  - pinned files changed only by whole-token upstream-version substitution;
  - check files whose existing lines change only by version substitution, whose inserted lines fully match the signed `check_insertion_pattern` (expansion-free changelog assertions), with no insertion after a continued line and no hidden line-break characters;
  - in-place modifications only;
  - an OWNER/MEMBER request issue and same-repo PR with green checks and preflight, its release hold, no auto-merge and no `needs-maintainer-review`.
- **Where it is re-proved:** the policy is re-verified after re-reading its body, again as the final authorization step, and again at the exact head immediately before merge.
- **Merge guard:** `release_authorize` accepts the policy only for the matching exact head.
- **What never uses it:** stale or unverifiable per-release signatures never fall back to the policy. An already-merged head resumes publication verification only and does not claim policy authority.
- **Moved heads:** under an active policy, an unsigned request whose head moved is retired after re-verification, so a fresh exact-head request follows.
- **Revocation:** close, edit or comment on the policy issue.

Without a signed policy, behaviour is unchanged.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py, .agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh, .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-packaging.md, .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md

## Decisions

- **Opt-in and signed per repository:** the security boundary stays a maintainer signature. Snapshot staleness gives revocation by edit, comment or close.
- **Check files are constrained:** they decide the preflight verdict, so existing lines may change only by version substitution and new lines must match the signed pattern.
- **Pinned files are tighter:** they substitute only the upstream version, because a token equal to the package version may be an unrelated dependency pin.
- **Compare base:** the merge-base compare uses the resolved `main` SHA, because a squash merge applies that diff.
- **Independent security review:** there were two rounds.
  - Round 1 found 1 high and 3 medium issues, all fixed.
  - Round 2 returned ready-with-followups (N1 hidden line breaks, N2 revocation during the proof, N3 package-version tokens in pinned files, plus a 0.x minor bump and insertion after a continued line). All of these are fixed in 7581d57eec, with regression tests.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified.
  - **Live runtime check (read-only):** the real `release_policy_authorizes` path ran against the GitHub API for marcusquinn/aidevops-cloudron-app PR #250 (head 16aa570), with only the signed-policy lookup simulated using the helper's real default policy. It returned `routine` at the final head. That run exercised the PR snapshot, release hold, checks/preflight, the open trusted finding #249, the resolved main SHA, the merge-base compare, exact-head contents and the predicate.
  - **Orchestration tests:** merge and publish orchestration are covered by `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` with stubbed gh/verify: 155 PASS, 0 FAIL. Coverage includes the policy process and authorize paths, 37 predicate cases and 19 authorization plumbing cases (including revocation during the proof), policy-request idempotence, and confirmation that signed or non-canonical policies are never rewritten.
  - **Static checks:** shellcheck is clean, py_compile is clean, and the function-complexity and file-size ratchets show no new violations.
  - **Fail-closed behaviour:** `approval-helper.sh verify` prints `NO_APPROVAL` only after a successful comment read with zero markers. API failures print `API_ERROR`.
  - **Scope:** no policy has been signed, and nothing has been merged or published in any package repo.

Resolves #37697

title: t18964: release stale fixed-path worktree reservations (GH#37706)
body:
## Summary

Fixed-path worktree producers (Buzz host agents) re-create a tree at the same path, e.g. `${worktree_base}/<repo>-buzz-<host>-<agent>`. When an earlier generation's tree vanished before retirement finished, its closed admission kept the unique path reservation. Enrollment of the replacement then refused with `reserved-path-without-enrollment-marker`, so the Buzz agent could not start ("Worktree retained: generation enrollment failed").

## Changes

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/path_release.py` (new):
  - `release_vacant_path`: while the path is absent, runs the existing fenced `absence.reconcile_absence` for the reserving generation. No-ops: `no-reservation`, `path-present`.
  - `release_replaced_path`: operator recovery when a replacement already occupies the path. Eligible only when the linked tree has no generation marker, the reserving generation has no planned retirement, and every bound run was admitted and has ended. Previews by default; `--confirm` journals `replaced-path-released` evidence and releases the reservation in one writer transaction. Deletes no files, archives or Git data.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py`: CLI subcommands `release-vacant-path` and `release-replaced-path [--confirm]`.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh`: `worktree_create_registered` calls `release-vacant-path` before creation (best-effort, skipped for private/disabled workloads); enrollment refusals for this case print the operator remediation.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/ABSENCE.md`: new "Fixed-path reuse (GH#37706)" section; `CLEANUP.md` pointer updated.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_path_release.py`: 9 tests for eligibility refusals (live/unknown owners, planned retirement, marker present), preview vs confirm, and the vacant-path path.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_path_release -v` → 9 passed
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_absence tests.test_enrollment tests.test_creation` → 76 passed, 2 skipped
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_path_release tests.test_absence` after the doc move → 27 passed
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh` → clean
- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-worktree.mjs` → 1 passed
- Live recovery on the affected host using this branch's CLI:
  - `release-replaced-path` preview → `replaced-path-preview`; `--confirm` → `replaced-path-released`
  - deployed `enroll --initialize --allow-schema-1-observation` → new generation; `reuse-status` → `eligible`
  - second stale path: `release-vacant-path` → `source-absent-reconciled` (`source-disappeared`)

## Scope notes

- The stale-branch observation from the issue (a fixed-path branch far behind `origin/main`) is not addressed here; it is a refresh-policy question, not a lifecycle reservation defect.
- `release-replaced-path` does not archive or remove the replacement tree; it only releases the stale reservation so the replacement can enroll and later retire through the normal archive-first executor.

Resolves #37706

title: fix(tabby): serialize SSH authentication during bulk restore
body:
## Summary

Ref #37552. Follow-up to the earlier bulk restore fix: desktop testing again required multiple invocations to attach all requested sessions. SSH daemon diagnostics confirmed pre-authentication connection drops with a restrictive `PerSourceMaxStartups` limit. Removing redundant probes alone does not serialize the remaining interactive handshakes.

- Serialize managed SSH authentication per locally resolved hostname/port, including different usernames on the same listener.
- Release the private local lock when the existing remote attachment marker proves authentication completed, while already-connected sessions remain alive.
- Coordinate inventory and creation probes with the same authentication slot. Read-only list/doctor/dry runs use existing lock state without initializing it.
- Preserve stable session leases, duplicate prevention, legacy resolution, and final remote identity checks. Do not change SSH daemon policy, credentials, or user SSH configuration.

## Implementation context

- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_auth.py`: new authentication-slot context manager built on the existing secure state directory and lease primitives; keep the lock inode and release descriptors on startup/failure/cancellation paths.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_config.py`: reuse local OpenSSH configuration resolution to group authentication by listener rather than username/session identity.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_transport.py`: integrate the slot with the existing remote-marker callback; release before waiting for the attached session to exit.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_sessions.py`: coordinate inventory/new-session operations and explicit remote doctor probes without holding the lock while launching GUI requests.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-sessions.py`: extend the existing unittest runner with lock lifecycle, read-only behavior, listener grouping, failure cleanup, and 20 queued connections.
- `.agents/tools/terminal/remote-sessions.md`: document queue behavior and limits. External programs, different local state directories/accounts, and distinct DNS names resolving to one listener are not coordinated.

## Runtime Testing

Testing level: **self-assessed** for the production desktop workflow. Unit/concurrency checks execute the implementation locally; they are not a live Tabby/OpenSSH end-to-end test.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-session-helper.sh`: **70 tests passed**, including the shell launcher path.
- The 20-connection concurrency case observes a peak of one pending handshake while all 20 simulated connected sessions remain alive.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: available checks passed; Markdown lint unavailable because markdownlint is not installed.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Pre-commit checks passed without bypasses.

Runtime risk: **medium**. This changes SSH/session scheduling. Interactive authentication can intentionally hold the queue until it completes or is cancelled. Server security policy remains unchanged.

## Desktop acceptance — draft until verified

Install/test this source checkout on the machine actually running Tabby; updating only the remote host does not update the desktop restore code.

1. Run one restore and complete normal Tabby Run/authentication prompts. Let queued handshakes finish rather than repeatedly restoring.
2. Observe with list until every expected session is connected; a launch request is not proof of attachment.
3. Repeat restore and confirm already-connected managed attachments are skipped without duplicate tabs.
4. Confirm that different listeners can authenticate independently and no server configuration changes are required.

Live desktop acceptance remains pending. This draft does not claim the production restore defect is solved and is not authorization to merge or publish a release.

title: fix(lifecycle): add opt-in protected process inspection
body:
## Summary

Add a default-off, operator-installed observation path for protected same-user Linux processes without relaxing registry retirement checks.

A protected SSH process newer than the candidate worktree cannot use the existing predating-daemon exception. The legacy CWD-only diagnostic can report complete visibility while the registry's stricter thread/CWD/file-descriptor census still refuses retirement. A CWD-only response or legacy lifetime receipt must not fill that evidence gap.

## Implementation and review scope

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/protected_proc.py`: opt-in adapter, trusted fixed inspector path and resolved sudo executable, root-owned/non-writable executable ancestry, bounded noninteractive execution, strict versioned response validation, and fresh process/candidate identity binding. NixOS and explicit maintenance remain unprivileged.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-cwd-inspect.py`: preserve the legacy single-PID CWD interface; add `--references PID CANDIDATE` for every thread's CWD and file descriptors. Reject foreign ownership, incomplete inventories and changing identities. Return only bound `clear`/`held` evidence, never reference paths or deletion authority. Bound the inspector child itself to two seconds and the caller's wait to three seconds.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/{legacy_proc,cli_errors,cleanup_failure}.py` and `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`: preserve normal native observation and fail-closed behavior; expose path-free PID/TID, stage and refusal diagnostics through targeted and collected failures.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py`: include the new adapter in the existing registry validation bundle.
- Existing inspector and retirement-process tests: cover private-thread CWD/FD holders, identity changes, incomplete and stale responses, ownership/trust checks, timeout, opt-out and platform restrictions.
- `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md` and `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`: document the distinct observation contracts, opt-in and operator installation boundary.

The reference pattern remains the existing native census plus the existing restricted, standalone root-owned inspector. No new runner, registry, fixture service or CI gate is introduced.

Independent design consultation identified an ambiguous ` (deleted)` suffix: it can be a literal live filename as well as a kernel annotation. Both matchers now conservatively check raw and suffix-stripped forms, with regression coverage. That consultation was not privileged runtime verification or installation approval.

## Safety and acceptance boundaries

- `AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_PROC_INSPECTION=1` is required; default behavior remains unprivileged and conservative.
- Source publication does not install or upgrade the root-owned component, modify sudo policy, stop SSH, or authorize retirement. An older installed inspector rejects the new mode and the worktree remains held.
- Do not run a writable source-checkout inspector through sudo. Any installation needs separate explicit operator authority and review of the expanded scope.
- Unknown, partial, timed-out or identity-mismatched observations retain the source. Existing ownership, admission, preservation and repeated retirement-boundary checks remain intact.
- A successful response describes a fresh bounded census, not an atomic snapshot, future-writer exclusion, reusable lifetime proof or cleanup permit.
- This draft publishes source for review only. No privileged installation, protected-process invocation, real worktree retirement or downstream deployment is claimed. Those acceptance steps remain separate.

## Verification

Passed on the committed head `256ae5d8f2f35fcced519c327e8b45efc3cf35d4`:

- 55 focused lifecycle, bundle, event and failure-diagnostic tests.
- 17 inspector tests, including legacy interface compatibility and bounded reference-mode behavior.
- Ruff 0.11.13 and mypy 1.15.0; mypy checked 50 source files.
- Changed-file quality gates, ShellCheck, secret scanning and whitespace checks.
- Normal pre-commit and pre-push hooks, including the repository's Bun typecheck; no hook bypass.

The production reference-report function was also exercised without privilege against the invoking process: it reported the current worktree as held and an unrelated owned directory as clear. This does not establish behavior against a protected SSH process or the installed privileged CLI.

Reproduce the focused Python checks from `.agents/worker-lifecycle/`:

```bash
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_legacy_cleanup.LegacyProcContract tests.test_retirement_processes tests.test_bundle tests.test_events tests.test_failure_category
```

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 -B .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py
ruff check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle .agents/scripts/worktree-cwd-inspect.py .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py
mypy --config-file .agents/worker-lifecycle/mypy.ini
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
```

Use the pinned development-tool versions above and session-owned disposable temporary storage for the existing test fixtures.

## Verification limitations

- `tests.test_legacy_cleanup.LegacyCleanupContract.test_interrupted_removal_resumes_after_git_deleted_its_link` fails with `proc-observation-unavailable` in both the candidate and the untouched baseline at `7eba8fd561bf41ed5c4c04411b74a4357f9f4ba2`. The relevant legacy test and observer/runner sources match the candidate's base. This existing failure was not suppressed or repaired here.
- A broader legacy batch exceeded 120 seconds. A separate four-test retirement batch exceeded 90 seconds after its first two tests reported success. Neither batch is claimed fully green.
- Markdownlint was unavailable locally. The quality runner also reported a pre-existing shfmt advisory in `worker-lifecycle-state.sh`; unrelated formatting was left untouched.
- No installed-helper, protected-SSH, privileged security-boundary, macOS hardware or actual retirement qualification is claimed by these local results. Maintainer security review and required CI results remain outstanding.

title: GH#37759: ci: install pinned shfmt release binary instead of apt in Complexity Analysis
body:
## Summary

The required `Complexity Analysis` check now installs `shfmt` from the pinned upstream release binary instead of Ubuntu apt.

Since about 13:47Z today, every `Code Quality Analysis` run has failed at `Install shfmt` with `Temporary failure resolving 'azure.archive.ubuntu.com'`. That includes main (run 43032307799) and PR #37736 (three attempts). Because the check is required, the mirror outage blocked every substantive PR.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, job `complexity-check`, step `Install shfmt (for nesting-depth AST scanner, GH#20105)`:

- Downloads `shfmt_v3.8.0_linux_amd64` from `mvdan/sh` GitHub releases. v3.8.0 is the version the apt package installed (`shfmt_3.8.0-1`), so `--to-json` AST output and scanner results don't change.
- Checks SHA-256 `27b3c6f9…b558fe0` with `sha256sum --check --strict` before install, so any byte change fails the step. Upstream doesn't publish a digest for v3.8.0. I computed this one from the release asset; it is a statically linked x86-64 Go ELF.
- Bounds the download with `curl --retry 5 --retry-all-errors`, `--connect-timeout 15 --max-time 45` and a 5-minute step timeout. The old step allowed 2 × 300 s apt phases plus a heartbeat helper.
- Removes the apt-source pruning and `run_with_heartbeat` from this step only. Nothing else referenced them (`git grep` found no other uses).

Out of scope: the non-required `Model replay verifier boundary (ubuntu-22.04)` job still installs Bubblewrap through apt (no upstream binary release; noted in #37759).

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/code-quality.yml`: no findings in the changed step. The one remaining SC2016 info is pre-existing at line 578.
- Local checksum check: the correct digest reports `OK` and a one-character mutation reports `FAILED`.
- This PR's own `Complexity Analysis` run (job 130631313201) passed on the new step during the apt DNS outage. The step log shows `<RUNNER_TEMP>/shfmt: OK` and `v3.8.0`, with no `apt-get` lines. `Shell function complexity` and `Shell nesting depth` both passed.
- The non-required `Model replay verifier boundary (ubuntu-22.04)` job still fails at `Install Bubblewrap` with the same DNS error. This PR doesn't touch that job.

## Regression Evidence

This change only affects how a GitHub-hosted CI step gets a tool. A repository test can't reproduce hosted-runner apt mirror DNS or the release download, so the regression evidence is the job itself: every PR touching this workflow runs the changed `Complexity Analysis` step. If the download or checksum breaks, the required check fails closed with `sha256sum: FAILED`. It doesn't fall back to the legacy AWK scanner. The passing run above, during the outage that broke the apt path, is the before/after evidence.

Resolves #37759

title: GH#37780: fix(pulse): honour foreign-owned active-claim hints on empty-pool runners
body:
## Summary

On a multi-runner fleet, a runner with an empty local worker pool ignored every cached `dedup_active_claim*` hint. It re-ran the full `dispatch_with_dedup` ceremony (about 36 s each) on issues that other runners already held. That used up the cycle's 600 s dispatch reserve, so nothing launched and the pool stayed empty, which kept the cache disabled.

This change keeps the authoritative recheck for claims this runner could own (self-assigned, mixed, or unknown self login). It honours the existing bounded hint when every assignee is another runner.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: new `_dispatch_claim_owned_elsewhere` helper. Inside the `dedup_active_claim*` case of `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`, an empty pool returns the hint only for foreign-owned candidates. An unset or malformed `_DISPATCH_SELF_LOGIN` fails closed to the previous behaviour.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: exports `_DISPATCH_SELF_LOGIN` from the already-resolved `self_login` in `dispatch_max`. Other entry points leave it unset and keep the old behaviour.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`: empty-pool assertions:
  - foreign owner returns a hit;
  - self, mixed self+foreign and unassigned return a miss;
  - unset or malformed self login returns a miss;
  - a non-empty pool still returns a hit.

Unchanged: the owner/status-label gate, the TTL (≤1800 s), `updatedAt` invalidation, `_dispatch_recheck_zero_worker_active_claims`, and every guard inside `dispatch_with_dedup`. A dead foreign claim is still rechecked authoritatively at least every 30 minutes, or immediately on any issue update.

## Evidence

One runner over about 6 h on 2026-11-11:

- 42 budget-skipped rounds; 50 of 60 health summaries show `dispatched=0` against a 20-worker target.
- 56 `dedup_active_claim` ceremonies took 33.7 min.
- All 9 distinct issues behind those ceremonies were owned by two other runners.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (dispatch dedup hint; launch guards unchanged)

title: GH#37811: fix(pulse): release an unadmittable main-dispatch reserve so pre-dispatch stages stop starving
body:
## Summary

Pre-dispatch Pulse stages were deferred to protect the main-dispatch reserve even after the main round could no longer be admitted that cycle. The reserve then protected nothing, while the stale-queued-run watchdog, orphan reaper, dependency graph and blocked-status refresh all starved.

## Evidence

On the Mac runner's `pulse.log`:

- `stale_queued_runs` was deferred 186 times. It last ran about 44h ago, when REST was exhausted. A `marcusquinn/aidevops` run queued since 2026-11-09 is still queued, which is exactly what the 8h watchdog should clear.
- `reap_orphan_workers` was deferred 186 times, `build_dependency_graph_cache` and `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` 179 each, and `dirty_pr_sweep` 175.
- Dispatch_max was skipped before enumeration 417 times. In each of the last 40 skips, `remaining` was below 780s, the bounded-census admission minimum (floor 600 + margin 60 + census 120). The stage reserve is 1110s.

## Change

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`: new `_pulse_main_dispatch_round_unadmittable` reuses `_dispatch_round_budget_plan before`. `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout` applies `_PULSE_MAIN_DISPATCH_RESERVE_S` only while the round can still be admitted, and logs `Stage dispatch reserve released: <stage>` otherwise. When the library or clock is unavailable, the GH#37051 reserve is kept.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: `assert_stage_cycle_budget_contract` gains an `unadmittable` case (710s left, so the stage runs with 600s). The existing `protected` case, where a full census still fits, still defers.

Cycle length is unchanged in practice. Stage timeouts remain clamped to the finalisation reserve, and cycles already use 1145–1700s of their 1800s budget (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: 87 tests, 0 failures. With only the production change stashed, the new case fails (`unadmittable:` empty), so the test catches the regression.
- `test-runner-capability.sh`, `test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh` and `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` pass.
- `test-permission-block-breaker.sh` exits 1 after its last PASS line both with and without this change. The failure is pre-existing and unrelated.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean on both files.

Resolves #37811

## Summary

Copied/migrated linked worktrees failed with an opaque StoreConflict. The session helper now reports the safe token generation-directory-mismatch, and OpenCode (lifecycle-admission.mjs) and Claude Code (git_safety_lifecycle.py) show non-destructive recovery guidance. New worktree-rescue-helper.sh (inspect/export/import/verify) moves uncommitted work out of a refused worktree without modifying it (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; index and status fingerprints checked before/after) into a fresh worktree at the same commit, with byte-exact verification. New reference/machine-migration.md documents old-machine-first and new-machine rescue paths plus interrupted recovery; pointers from REGISTRY.md and domain-index.md. Admission, enrollment, markers and cleanup authority are unchanged. Guarded retirement of rescued copies is tracked in #37828.

## Decisions

Kept the existing generation-directory-mismatch token rather than splitting by cause to avoid changing protocol strings other callers may match. Rescue uses a portable bundle (patch + untracked tar + hashes) instead of dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh because that tool restores in place to canonical checkouts, while migration needs cross-worktree and cross-machine transfer. Ignored files are listed, not copied, because they can hold secrets or be large. Read-only inspection needed no gate change: git -C read-only verbs from an outside workdir were already admitted without ownership (GH#37022); the guidance now says so.

title: GH#37862: promote starved prefetch ahead of early dispatch
body:
## Summary

Chosen design (spec step 1, run-before-early-dispatch option): a prefetch starvation bound. When STATE_FILE (pulse-state.txt) is missing or older than AIDEVOPS_PULSE_PREFETCH_STARVATION_S (default 7200s = 2h; 0 disables and restores legacy order), _run_preflight_stages runs the existing budget-gated prefetch stage before preflight_early_dispatch, so prefetch receives the full stage budget instead of the clamped remainder (105s in the evidence). Early dispatch still runs every cycle afterwards; promotion only happens while the snapshot is starved, and a successful prefetch rewrites STATE_FILE and ends promotion. The end-of-preflight prefetch is skipped when the promoted attempt already ran; a budget-deferred promoted attempt remains eligible for the legacy end-of-preflight attempt. A hard prefetch failure keeps its cycle-abort semantics but is applied only after the dispatch waves, matching the legacy position. A 124 timeout keeps the GH#34000 cached-state fallback. REST/GraphQL budget gates are unchanged. Files: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh (_preflight_prefetch_starved), .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh (_run_promoted_prefetch_if_starved, _PULSE_PREFETCH_RAN), .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh (assertions 11g/11g2/11h). title: GH#37869: reclaim ownerless ever-NMR cache locks
body:
## Summary

`_ever_nmr_cache_with_lock` only reclaimed a lock when `owner.pid` existed and named a dead PID. A lock directory with no `owner.pid` was never reclaimed. One pulse host held such a lock for 11 days: `pulse.log` logged 3111 lock timeouts, every negative cache entry expired, and every dispatch candidate fell through to the REST timeline API. This contributed to REST-core pacing and cooldown deferrals and to slow `dispatch_with_dedup` launches.

## Changes

`.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval-cache.sh` now follows the `audit-log-helper.sh` reclaim pattern. A lock is reclaimed when:

- **It has no owner:** no valid `owner.pid`, and the lock is older than `EVER_NMR_LOCK_ORPHAN_AGE_SECS` (default 60 seconds).
- **Its owner is dead:** existing behaviour, kept.

A live owner is never reclaimed. Legacy `$$` records come only from processes still running pre-fix code, and their locks fall to the dead-owner path once those processes exit.

Other changes:

- **One reclaimer at a time:** a `.reclaim` directory elects the reclaimer. The winner then re-checks the lock's instance token (directory inode plus owner record) and backs off if the lock was replaced in the meantime. A `.reclaim` left behind by a killed reclaimer is cleared once it is older than the orphan age, so it can't wedge the lock either.
- **Ownership checks:** if the owner write fails, ownership is treated as lost and the callback is skipped. Release removes the lock only when `owner.pid` still names the caller.
- **Owner PID:** the record now uses `BASHPID`, with the Bash 3.2 `exec sh` PPID fallback, instead of `$$`. It is resolved in the locking shell itself.
- **Settings:** they are read as base 10, so `08` is not treated as invalid octal. `EVER_NMR_LOCK_RETRIES` defaults to 50 (unchanged).
- **Still non-fatal:** `_ever_nmr_cache_set` still returns 0. Lock mtimes come from `portable-stat.sh` `_file_mtime_epoch`.

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-ever-nmr-cache.sh` now sources the production module instead of a private copy. It adds cases for:

- an old ownerless lock (reclaimed)
- a fresh ownerless lock (respected)
- a dead owner (reclaimed)
- an old live owner (respected)
- leading-zero settings (read as decimal)
- a lock re-acquired by another caller during release (left in place)
- a lost lock before owner registration (callback skipped)
- instance-token change detection
- an abandoned `.reclaim` marker (cleared)
- an owner PID written from a subshell (recorded correctly)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-ever-nmr-cache.sh`: 14/14 pass under Bash 5 and macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.
- `shellcheck` on both files: clean.
- Sibling suites `test-pulse-nmr-approval.sh` (34/34), `test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority.sh` (36/36) and `test-pulse-nmr-state-pruning.sh`: pass.
- After deploy: `pulse.log` should show no sustained `_ever_nmr_cache_with_lock: lock acquisition timed out` run, and the cache file mtime should keep advancing.

Resolves #37869
